text: Week 8+: The BaselineState: DeltaFosB degraded, if the animal timelines carry over. Hardware reset complete.
reader: someone eight weeks into the protocol asking whether the hard part is over

sentences.s: Week 8+: The BaselineState: DeltaFosB degraded, if the animal timelines carry over.
sentences.payoff: It tells the reader what Week 8 is for -- the protein they have been clearing is gone -- and, with the added clause, that the eight weeks is an estimate carried over from animal work, so if they are not there yet nothing has failed.
sentences.follows: It is the last phase of the timeline, after the Void phase of weeks 3 to 5, and it answers the question the whole timeline sets up: when is this over.

checked.found: Persistence of at least several weeks after the stimulus stops, half-life up to about 8 days in vivo, 28 days in the longest measurement (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8879420). No human de-armoring timeline exists, and nothing measures DeltaFosB clearing in a person on a protocol.
checked.still_needed: yes: eight weeks sits inside the sourced range, so the line keeps its point; what it cannot claim is that the date has been measured in people

placement: Last entry of Part 5, after Weeks 3-5. The phases run in the order the reader lives them, and this is the one they are reading for when they want to know whether the hard part is over.

questions.Q1: PASS: the week comes first, then the state, then the caveat on the week.
questions.Q2: N/A: the maintenance instructions are in the next line, his and unchanged.
questions.Q3: PASS: "the animal timelines" are the rodent persistence measurements, which the card names with their source.
questions.Q4: PASS: no new term. "Carry over" says what is uncertain -- species, not mechanism.
questions.Q5: PASS: "if" attaches the condition to the claim it qualifies.
questions.Q6: PASS: unchanged position at the end of the timeline.
questions.Q7: PASS: this reader is asking whether they are done; an unhedged date would have them judge themselves against a clock nobody has checked in people.
questions.Q8: PASS: belongs with the timeline phases.
questions.Q9: PASS: one added clause, no step compressed.

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone?
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
